additionalCoursework: Biochemistry 1 semester / 3 credits; Organic Chemistry (with lab) 2 semesters / 8 credits; Physics (with lab) 2 semesters / 8 credits; Ethics 1 semester / 3 credits; Behavioral Science 1 semester / 3 credits; Biostatistics 1 semester / 3 credits; Humanities 2 semesters / 6 credits; Spanish 2 semesters / 6 credits.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Cooper Medical School of Rowan University is committed to providing an environment that respects the contributions, talents, and varied experiences of all of our students, faculty, and staff. We embrace the philosophy that excellence in medical education, research, and clinical practice is best achieved through maintaining an academic and work environment free of discrimination. Our office of Engagement and Community Impact provides structured outreach programs for pre-college and college students, as well as ample resources and guidance to support the student body's initiatives.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence may be for either a defined or an undefined period of time, determined jointly by the associate dean of admissions and student affairs and the associate dean of medical education. Except in extraordinary circumstances, such as situations involving extended research, a student may request a leave of absence only for a period of up to one academic year. The student may request an extension to a leave of absence for extraordinary extenuating circumstances.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: CMSRU provides each student with the support and services needed to grow as a person and a health care provider. The Office of Student Affairs and the Office Engagement and Community Impact both serve as resources for a myriad of social, community, career, and mentoring groups.  Our Advisory Colleges become the hub for many student mentoring needs, providing a network of faculty advisors, peer-to-peer support, and social outlets.  Advisory College Directors are specially trained to provide guidance for educational needs, physical and emotional health, career choice, community service, and individual and group activities.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: CMSRU's Medical Education Building is designed around the innovative CMSRU curriculum, filled with spaces and technologies to support our faculty and students in this process.  This is a six-story, 200,000 square foot building, with an exterior designed to reflect the historic nature of the community while looking forward into the future.  27 Active Learning Rooms were designed to house Active Learning Groups of 8 students and 2 faculty members.  Approximately 75% of the CMSRU structured class time occurs in these small group settings, under the expert guidance of faculty partners: one clinician and one biomedical researcher.  Additionally, wet lab space, active research laboratories, a renowned Clinical Simulation Center provide students continual opportunities to build their scientific, clinical and interpersonal skills from the moment they enter CMSRU.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Furnished and unfurnished apartments are available for our students directly across from the medical education building. These units are singles, doubles and triples and our students have priority in assigning tenant status. Medical students are expected to make their own living arrangements. The Office of Student Affairs will publicize opportunities available to allow for a variety of safe and convenient living options.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Support systems for gender and sexual minority students are available through the Office of Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Support systems for applicants and learners with disabilities is available through the Office of Student Affairs and the Office of Medical Education.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Office of Student Affairs (OSA) at CMSRU, in collaboration with staff, faculty, and student leadership, has created a comprehensive system of programming to support students’ well-being and adjustment to the physical and emotional demands of medical school.

The OSA has adopted a culture of wellness that supplements students' classroom learning and contributes to their personal development through an array of programs, advisory college resources, and clubs/organizations designed to promote and sustain the wellbeing of our students. ​The OSA incorporates the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration's (SAMHSA) eight dimensions of wellness to offer programs and resources that align with each dimension of wellness, to best meet the needs of the student when providing supplemental information and facilitating wellness.  The SAMHSA eight dimensions of wellness include:
-Social
-Intellectual
-Physical
-Spiritual
-Environmental
-Emotional
-Financial
-Occupational/Academic  

Learn more at: https://cmsru.rowan.edu/student_life/mental-health-and-wellness/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Known as the , 'medical school with a soul', CMSRU is a community of students, faculty, and other practitioners throughout CMSRU and the Cooper University Health Care system dedicated to learning, practicing, and sharing humanistic healthcare practices. We achieve this through education and mentorship, research and publications, medical ethics programs, and consultation services. We promote empathy, respect, integrity, altruism, and the pursuit of excellence.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: It is recommended that by the 3rd year, students have regular access to a vehicle as they may need to drive to clinical sites.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: CMSRU provides each student with the support and services needed to grow as a person and a health care provider.  Students enjoy structured, layered mentoring and open-door access to CMSRU faculty.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: CMSRU students begin at the Ambulatory Clinic in the first week of the M1 year. They assume supervised responsibility for the primary care management of their patients, who will span all age groups.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Active learning, especially in small group settings, is emphasized.  Self-directed learning is encouraged and dedicated time for self-directed learning is embedded in the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Most required clinical clerkships take place at Cooper University Hospital.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: There is a required 7-week virtual course entitled Introduction to Medical Education that is planned to begin on June 14th.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance for most lecture sessions is not mandatory.  Most lectures are recorded.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Our curriculum arises from our mission and is designed to be a seamless continuum over four years, integrating knowledge of scientific concepts, early clinical experience and patient care, self-directed learning, teamwork, and activities for the greater community’s benefit.  Our students immediately apply basic scientific principles to clinical cases and patient care.  Our integrated approach to teaching puts biomedical scientists and clinicians together with our students, primarily in a small group setting, and students reflect on their experiences through self-directed inquiry.  Our focus on healthcare delivery, systems engineering, outcome-driven care, and cost containment prepares our graduates to thrive in a complex healthcare system, even as they reshape healthcare for the next generation.  

We offer an accelerated three-year track (PC3) for motivated students planning a career in Primary Care Internal Medicine or Pediatrics.  https://cmsru.rowan.edu/admissions/apply-to-cmsru/application-process/apply-to-pc3-program.html
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The Ambulatory Clerkship is a highlight of CMSRU's curriculum, providing both early and continuing clinical experiences for students and a significant benefit to the community. In the Ambulatory Clerkship, medical students will learn how to provide high quality primary care services to an underserved population of patients, and thereby reduce the healthcare disparities within that population. This clerkship is an experience that begins in the fifth week of medical school. The students assume supervised responsibility for the primary care management of their patients, who will span all age groups.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Structured research opportunities for medical students exist via several pathways.   Our clinical and basic science faculty are engaged in an array of publicly and privately funded research projects and successfully publish research articles in a variety of scholarly journals each year. Our faculty members are committed to mentoring medical students with specific research interests and providing opportunities for involvement in important scientific and medical research.  Applied clinical research, healthcare systems research, biomedical engineering opportunities, medical education research, and basic science laboratory opportunities are available to CMSRU students.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: All students are required to complete a capstone project as a component of the Scholars Workshop course.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: These are the M3 clinical training sites outside of Cooper University Healthcare:  Northbrook Behavioral Health Hospital (Psychiatry) Inspira Hospital  (Neurology) Advocare (Pediatrics).
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Tiered, competency-based grading system. Years 1-2 is Pass/Low Pass/Unsatisfactory, focusing on mastery. Years 3-4 uses Honors/High Pass/Pass/Unsatisfactory.  No High Pass in the fourth year.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Cooper Medical School of Rowan University initially received full Accreditation from the LCME in June of 2016 and received eight-year re-accreditation in 2021. The school opened in 2012 and has matriculated its eleventh class. The Class of 2031 will enroll 118 students. It is in the spirit of and driven by the CMSRU mission that the educational facilities for undergraduate medical education have been designed and developed. Located in Camden, NJ, one block from Cooper University Hospital, the building is a 203,000 square foot, six-story building designed to support the CMSRU curriculum.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Cooper Medical School of Rowan University is committed to providing humanistic education in the art and science of medicine within a scientific and scholarly community in which excellence in patient care, innovative teaching, scholarly activity and service to our community are valued.

Our core values include a commitment to: a positive learning environment, mentorship, professionalism, patient advocacy, wellness, the communities we serve, and scholarly activity.

Our Vision: Cooper Medical School of Rowan University will distinguish itself as an innovator in medical education and biomedical research that will lead to the transformation of healthcare.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: In partnership with Cooper Medical School of Rowan University (CMSRU)  Rowan University is proud to offer a 7-Year Medical School Program (also called 3+4 year program) to incoming first-year students. This rigorous, accelerated degree program provides an opportunity for exceptional students to apply to CMSRU during their junior year at Rowan and enter medical school in their fourth year. Students who successfully complete the program receive a Bachelor of Science (BS) degree (earned after successfully completing their first year of medical school or veterinary school) and a Doctor of Medicine (MD),  in seven years, rather than the traditional eight.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: At least two of the letters must be from academic faculty, and applicants should always request letters from professors or supervisors who know the candidate well.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: All letters of recommendation should be submitted through AMCAS Letters. CMSRU will not accept letters submitted outside of this system. CMSRU prefers, when possible, to receive a letter authored by a pre-health committee or advisor intended to represent your institution’s evaluation (many institutions extend this service to its graduates as well). This letter may include additional letters of support. If there is no pre-health committee or advisor at your school, you may submit individual letters of evaluation and recommendation through AMCAS Letters. We require a minimum of three letters.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Our interview day has been designed to provide each candidate the opportunity to engage with CMSRU faculty and students.  Throughout the day applicants interact with current students, and the finale provides a comfortable, casual meet-and-greet so that candidates can ask questions in a low-pressure and open atmosphere.  The interview day program includes:

   A virtual log-in and opportunity to meet the admissions staff.
   A live orientation and welcome with our Dean, Dr. Annette Reboli.
   A live question-and-answer session with the Office of Admissions leadership team.
   A live interview, lasting approximately 30 minutes.
   Live, informal meet-and-greet and question-and-answer sessions with our current students.

Available in advance are recorded presentations about our innovative curriculum, student support services, our simulation center and our three-year primary care track. A virtual tour of our medical school building is also available.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Held on Fridays. One interview with two interviewers: one who is on the Admissions Committee and one who is blinded to application materials, in addition to casual encounters with CMSRU students.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Admission policies and information for 2026-2027 Admissions Cycle

We know that some undergraduate institutions have changed academic courses to a pass/fail or pass/fail option and in the process have made laboratory components of those courses on-line. Although we have not previously accepted pre-requisite medical school courses taken on-line or pass/fail, we will allow both pass/fail grades and on-line courses for pre-requisites. 

As we conduct complete holistic review of applications, we encourage you to submit your AMCAS application if all other elements of your application are complete while you wait for your MCAT score to be available.  Our application deadline is November 15th, and our secondary application deadline is December 15th. 

Selection Criteria:  

Cooper Medical School of Rowan University (CMSRU) seeks students who demonstrate academic readiness, who resonate with our mission, and who possess the special personal attributes required of physicians.  More specifically, we are committed to selecting students who demonstrate a record of academic excellence, the potential to deliver competent and compassionate care, a passion for lifelong learning, intellectual curiosity, personal and professional integrity and ethical conduct, tolerance  and community-oriented service.  

Student selection is based on a holistic review of a candidate’s application and is not influenced by political or financial factors. To be eligible for admission, an applicant must be a citizen or permanent resident of the United States of America.  All applicants are required to complete a bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year college or university in the United States or Canada prior to enrollment in the MD Program.  CMSRU welcomes applicants with a wide-range of academic interests.  All majors are welcome to apply to CMSRU, as long as minimum academic requirements are met.  

CMSRU is seeking to recruit a student body that will add value to our school and contribute to the education of all students.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial Aid Services assists students in securing federal, state, and institutional aid to help meet the cost of pursuing an education at Cooper Medical School of Rowan University (CMSRU). Financing a medical education requires a great deal of planning and knowledge about resources. Students are encouraged to begin looking at the financial responsibilities of medical school as early as possible. As an educational debt management resource for students, the CMSRU Financial Aid Services staff strive to increase awareness and provide guidance to ensure CMSRU students become knowledgeable borrowers, as they pursue their education, residency and practice. Financial aid is not a factor in considering applicants for acceptance. Although financial aid is limited, CMSRU works closely with each student.  The Financial Aid Office guides the process of securing the scholarships, loans and loan forgiveness options to allow the student to pursue their career choice.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition and fees are payable in advance each semester, there is a monthly late payment fee of $50.00. A student may arrange with the Rowan University Bursar's Office to follow a deferred payment as follows: a. Payment of all fees plus one-half of the tuition before or upon registration. b. Payment of one-quarter of the tuition 30 days after the registration date and final one quarter 60 days after enrollment.

medSchoolPrograms.info: PULSE is a six week summer academic enrichment program for undergraduate students interested in pursuing a healthcare profession. This program provides academic, clinical, research and service learning opportunities with a focus on urban health needs. The primary goal of PULSE is to provide students  to medical professions.

CMSRU participates in a joint MD/PhD program with the Department of Biomedical Engineering in the Henry M. Rowan College of Engineering of Rowan University. The program is intended to consist of four years of medical education combined with three years of education in biomedical engineering.  Undergraduate experience in biomedical engineering is required to be considered for this program.  To be accepted into this program, applicants must independently successfully complete both the Rowan PhD and CMSRU MD program admissions processes.  Applicants to the program undergo the same screening, interview process, and admissions committee consideration as regular applicants to CMSRU. The CMSRU admissions committee is solely responsible for acceptance of applicants into the MD component of the MD/PhD program.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: CMSRU offers the accelerated three-year primary care track (PC3 track) for motivated students desiring a career in Family Medicine, Primary Care Internal Medicine, or Primary Care Pediatrics. After earning their Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree in three years, graduates will have the opportunity to complete their residency training in the residency program at Cooper and other institutions nationwide.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Candidates accepted to CMSRU are eligible to apply for the PC-3 track.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationDeadline: Our application cycle runs from August through March.  General PC-3 track invitations to apply are communicated through email up through March.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq: Must be an accepted CMSRU student to apply to this program.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Waitlist decisions occur on a rolling basis.  Acceptance offers generally begin in the spring of the application cycle under the direction of the Admissions Committee.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: All candidates must complete a Bachelor's degree from an accredited US or Canadian institution. Community college coursework is accepted for required courses, but we highly recommend taking additional upper level sciences at the 4-year college/university level to show continued academic success in those subjects. See our website for details. To be eligible for admission, applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents of the U.S.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: CMSRU students experience firsthand the benefits of learning in diverse groups, guided by faculty experts.  As CMSRU students engage with clinical vignettes or disparate educational backgrounds, cultural traditions, learning styles, and worldviews. Our admissions committee seeks candidates who will thrive in a team-based, self-directed learning environment, and who have demonstrated the drive to improve health care access in (urban) underserved populations. The successful candidate possesses solid academic preparation, well developed interpersonal skills, maturity, professionalism, and the capacity to make a positive impact on the CMSRU and Camden communities.  All application materials (including letters of recommendation) must be submitted via AMCAS.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Candidates are strongly encouraged to gain experience in a clinical setting, but formal shadowing is not required.  Successful applicants can discuss their clinical exposure in a meaningful context, providing evidence that they can assimilate varied experiences into their professional and personal growth.
